problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 11 & 1 & 19 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Many Zeros
examples.problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14081590/assets/28a22a5f860f02e42abc699e9807de885cc01b572c23ac0d4f909fe281042e08.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Notice that the $1$st column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 13 & 19 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 2 & 0 \\ 13 & 19 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 2 & 0 \\ 13 & 19 & -3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 2 & 0 \\ 13 & 19 & -3\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot 2\cdot (-3)=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\det(A) = 2 \cdot (-6) = -12.
$$

feedback.problem: Given that $E=5I$, where $I$ is the $3\times 3$ identity matrix, what is the value of $det(E)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}5I & =5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a diagonal matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & =5\cdot 5\cdot 5=125.\end{aligned}
$$
